findings.title: An independent fresh clone at the same absolute path as the implement checkout is refused with E_SELF_REVIEW
findings.x-evidence: Real CLI, scratch implement clone plus bare remote: a fresh clone at the SAME absolute path passes receive review (exit 0). The implement checkout is still denied (exit 3 E_SELF_REVIEW) as-is, after deleting .baton/.local/session.json, and after git clean -xfd. A second git worktree passes; its identity lives at .git/worktrees/<name>/baton/checkout-id. The F88 one-cycle override still works: receive passes after the token is deleted, and after review routes to work and a new work write, the same checkout is denied again. Copying .git/baton/checkout-id into another clone makes that clone stricter (denied), not a bypass. Deleting both the token and the git identity in the implement checkout passes; that is a deliberate double deletion of documented files and is accepted for a process guard.

findings.title: Deleting the token and invoking through an alias path (junction, symlink, 8.3, subst) bypasses the worktree check
findings.x-evidence: With the token deleted, receive review through a junction alias, the 8.3 short path and a subst drive of the implement checkout all exit 3 E_SELF_REVIEW. The identity comes from git rev-parse --git-path, so it doesn't depend on the path spelling. The automated alias assertion is weak (see F118).

findings.title: The committed x-worktree / x-implementation-worktree is an unsalted sha256 of the absolute path, so the OS username can be recovered
findings.x-evidence: New entries hash a random 32-byte identity: the quick baton's x-worktree 460f84d3... matches no path candidate. Legacy values already committed in the feature baton remain; F112 tracks them.

findings.title: Manifest integrity uses normalized hashes in doctor/adopt/models and raw digests in update/uninstall/init; a CRLF overlay checkout cannot update
findings.x-evidence: Overlay init, then a core.autocrlf=true clone (42 of 83 managed files CRLF). The c85bf3f CLI gives update --dry-run exit 4 with 42 conflicts, and uninstall keeps the files with W_USER_MODIFIED. The new CLI: doctor is clean apart from W_PACK_RECOMMENDED, update --dry-run and a real update exit 0 with 0 conflicts, 0 actions and no git changes, and uninstall exits 0, removes every managed file except the preserved constitution and removes the BATON marker. Integrity stays raw-byte strict: a CRLF-converted locked file gives lock verify E_LOCK_MISMATCH exit 1, build.mjs --check on a CRLF bundle exits 1, and the init payload lock check (init.mjs:186) still uses the raw digest. No payload file contains CRLF, so existing manifests remain valid.

findings.title: `models apply` on CRLF agent files now fails hard with E_FRONTMATTER_MALFORMED (regression from normalized isUserModified)
findings.x-evidence: On the autocrlf clone the c85bf3f CLI gives models apply --force E_FRONTMATTER_MALFORMED exit 1. The new CLI changes 9 agents; the files stay pure CRLF (no bare LF), and doctor stays clean afterwards.

findings.title: A corrupt checkout token or missing quick baton surfaces as E_INTERNAL (exit 10)
findings.x-evidence: session.json containing null, null with CRLF, [], "x", 42, {} or truncated JSON gives E_CHECKOUT_TOKEN exit 2. A missing quick baton gives E_USAGE exit 2 with the handoff new --quick remediation.

findings.title: `update` merges .gitattributes inside the per-entry loop: dry-run repeats the action per file and the merge is skipped when every entry continues
findings.x-evidence: update --dry-run lists exactly one merge .gitattributes. With every managed entry modified (82 conflicts, exit 4), the attributes block is still merged, in dry-run and in a real run. Moving the merge after the loop introduced F114.

findings.title: adopt removes the whole .baton/quick/ directory, deleting adopter-authored quick batons, and plan.md's disposition does not list it

The adopter creates .baton/quick/my-own-fix.md before cleanup runs, for example on the documented fallback path where the cleanup workflow cannot push and the adopter runs baton adopt later. adopt --dry-run lists remove .baton/quick/, and a real adopt --no-workflows deletes the whole directory, including the adopter's baton (adopt.mjs:270-274 rm -r). update and uninstall keep adopter quick batons, and adopt on an overlay repo is a no-op. template-cleanup.yml:2 cites plan.md 'Template disposition' as its source, but plan.md:180 does not list .baton/quick/.

findings.title: After code changes, a feature baton at review → land is stranded: land stops with E_STALE_REVIEW and no command returns it to review
findings.x-evidence: PR 30 changed code after the feature 001 review. In a fresh clone at a755ff8, handoff receive --phase land --feature 001-baton-template exits 1 with E_STALE_REVIEW, and receive --phase review exits 1 with E_TRANSITION ('Expected land'). The land contract allows next compound/done only, and no handoff action rewinds land to review. error-codes.md:24 says to review the changed tree again but gives no command. The same trap hits any adopter who commits a fix after review, for example a CI fix during land. Verified workaround: at the reviewed tree c85bf3f, after npm ci, the same receive --phase land exits 0. So feature 001 can land from a checkout at c85bf3f, and this quick lane covers c85bf3f..main; the owner needs to decide.
findings.reason: Resolved by the owner decision, option (a), received through Copilot: feature 001 lands at its reviewed tree c85bf3f and this quick lane (pretag-fixes-001) covers the post-review delta c85bf3f..main. The decision is recorded in the feature 001 land handoff in PR #32 (open, specs/001-baton-template/handoff.md only), which also backlogs option (b), a CLI route from a stale land back to review, for v0.2. This quick baton records the route as D15. No specs/ edit in this lane.

findings.title: A .gitattributes marker conflict now throws after update has rewritten managed files, leaving the manifest stale
findings.x-evidence: mergeAttributes throws E_CONFLICT on an unbalanced BATON marker. After F101 the throw happens after the per-entry loop's putBytes (update.mjs:159) and before writeManifest. The correctness persona reproduced it: the throw leaves a rewritten spec-template.md, and the next update reports that file as user-modified (exit 4). At c85bf3f the throw came before any managed write. This regression came from this pass.
findings.x-evidence-review2: c142fb7: update.mjs computes mergeAttributes before the per-entry loop (preflight) and keeps the single action/write after it. Real CLI on an overlay repo with an outdated owned spec-template.md and .gitattributes = "# BATON:START\n* text=auto\n": exit 4 E_CONFLICT, spec-template.md untouched, manifest byte-identical, no .baton/conflicts written. The a755ff8 bundle on the same setup rewrote spec-template.md (the regression). After repairing .gitattributes, update succeeds with 0 conflicts and doctor/uninstall are ok. Testing persona: restoring the a755ff8 update.mjs and rebuilding fails the new test at the owned-file assertion.

findings.title: checkoutHash silently drops the identity on any git exit 128 and leaves a stale x-implementation-worktree
findings.reason: Exit 128 from safe.directory 'dubious ownership', a bad GIT_DIR or a non-git root returns null with no warning. The guard then compares only the token, and handoff.mjs:720 keeps the previous cycle's x-implementation-worktree. Review and land writes still need git (reviewedTree), so the practical gap is receive in an unusual environment, for a process guard that is not a security boundary. Accepted for v0.1; recommend a W_ warning or a narrower null path later.

findings.title: Every handoff action fails with E_INTERNAL when the git dir is not writable
findings.reason: Reproduced by the adversarial persona with an icacls deny on .git: handoff next and receive give E_INTERNAL EPERM exit 10. Supported environments (local, Codespaces, Copilot cloud agent, Actions) have writable .git. Accepted for v0.1; later, map EACCES/EPERM/EROFS to an actionable error and skip identity creation for read-only actions.

findings.title: Batons written before this pass lose the worktree guard, so deleting the token re-enables self-review

Here only feature 001 is affected, and it is already past review. Accepted; mention re-handing off in-flight batons in future upgrade notes.

findings.title: template-cleanup.yml now hard-codes the source quick-baton filenames; the next source quick lane committed to main would ship to adopters and fail their first validate

Release precondition for the v0.1 tag and every later tag: git ls-files .baton/quick at the tagged commit must be a subset of template-cleanup.yml remove. Follow-up for v0.2: a source-repo guard test (beside review-fix-docs.test.mjs keep_dormant check) that every tracked .baton/quick/* is listed, and derive the adopt test literals from the config.

findings.title: A non-attributes error later in the update loop (E_PATH on a symlinked or junctioned managed path) still leaves earlier managed writes with a stale manifest
findings.reason: Pre-existing and outside the F114 scope; needs an adopter to junction a managed directory, which Baton refuses by design (E_PATH). Behavior is fail-closed except for manifest staleness that surfaces as a conflict on the next update. Backlog for v0.2: two-phase update (read and compute all entries, then write) or persist the manifest for entries already written before rethrow.

findings.title: A UTF-8 BOM before the Baton block in .gitattributes makes every update, including --dry-run, fail with a false Unbalanced BATON marker conflict and an empty file field
findings.reason: Pre-existing: the same throw existed before F114, which only moved it earlier. The block regex anchors ^# BATON:START and a leading U+FEFF defeats it. Rare (editor-added BOM on a git config file) and fails closed with nothing written. Backlog for v0.2: strip and restore a leading BOM, and set file .gitattributes plus a fix hint on the E_CONFLICT.
